text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1798765432 — KV cache pressure detected on shard set 7. p95/p99 of model-streaming requests spiking, some streaming stalls observed. Auto-alert to #eng-sre. :rotating_light:

alex: seeing p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.8s on a subset of hosts, p99 up to ~4.6s. Streaming sessions dropping around token 512 usually.

maria: confirmed. tail latency graphs show clear step starting ~08:14 UTC. KV cache eviction rate jumped ~3x.

jamal: key metric: kv_prefill_rate spiked and kv_decode_throughput dropped. Looks like prefill threads starving decode workers.

alex: any customer errors? I see some 502s and aborted streams from a few tenants — not full on outage yet but SLOs are breached for streaming p99.

sarah: customer-impact check: Support reported two customers with large chat sessions complaining about stalls. I've opened a ticket and assigned to SE team.

maria: quick mitigation idea: limit concurrent prefill workers on affected nodes (reduce `PREFILL_PARALLELISM` from 8 -> 4) to rebalance CPU for decode threads. Might help immediate tail.

jamal: agree. also can we temporarily disable aggressive prefetch for the most aggressive tenant IDs (route policy label `heavy-prefetch`) ?

alex: firing the following on affected hosts: 
```bash
sudo systemctl set-environment PREFILL_PARALLELISM=4
sudo systemctl restart redwood-prefill.service
```
I’ll roll to a single rack first.

incident-bot: NOTE — rate limit and quota controllers unaffected. No config change to routing policies yet.

ops-bot: Started cordon of host ip-10-2-7-45 for testing. Draining new long-lived streams.

maria: after first rack change, p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 650ms. p99 from 4.6s -> 1.2s on those hosts. Decent improvement.

jamal: good. but eviction rate still elevated — seems slab fragmentation on KV cache contributing to slow prefetch lookups. We might need a slab compaction in next maintenance window.

alex: short-term: continue rolling PREFILL_PARALLELISM change across affected racks plus reduce `KV_PREFILL_BATCH_SIZE` from 256 -> 128 for the hot model to lower allocation spikes.

maria: note — smaller batch size increases decode CPU slightly but should reduce eviction churn.

jamal: starting gradual rollout of the two-tweak plan now. Patch posted to ops repo: https://internal.redwood/ops/kv-prefill-rollout/1798765432 (internal).

sarah: reached out to the two impacted customers with ETA ~ 30-45m. Let them know we’re mitigating; no data loss risk.

alex: small regression observed on one host after the change — decode queue length rose for a moment then steadied. Watching.

maria: streaming stalls decreased by ~70% cluster-wide after 3 racks. p99 still slightly above SLO on some older GPU instances.

jamal: plan B if this doesn't fully resolve: route heavy streaming traffic to dedicated pools (redwood-dedicated-streams) for affected tenants while we run slab defrag on the host pool. That requires coordination with infra — will need 10-15m to shift routes.

alex: creating a temporary routing rule now for tenant tag `enterprise-heavy` -> `redwood-dedicated-streams`.

ops-bot: Route change posted, waiting for approval from infra-oncall.

maria: infra-oncall approved — starting route shift. Expect ~3-5% traffic shift per minute to avoid cache warm-up storms.

jamal: watch for cold-start spike in latencies on the dedicated side — we'll ramp slowly. Also ensure fallback policy still allows older model variants.

sarah: customer update: one impacted customer acknowledged the routing note and asked for a postmortem.

alex: current cluster numbers: overall p95 = 720ms, p99 = 1.4s, streaming error rate down from 0.8% -> 0.25%. Eviction rate trending down but slab fragmentation metric `kv_slab_free_runs` is still 30% below normal.

maria: logging snippet from an affected host: 
```
[08:21:03] kv.prefill: batch_size=256 -> evict_count=42 mem_free=1.2GB slab_frag_pct=47
[08:21:04] kv.decode: worker_blocked=true queue_len=18
[08:21:06] streaming: stall detected token_index=512 session_id=abc123
```

jamal: action items while oncall: 
- Alex: finish PREFILL_PARALLELISM + KV_PREFILL_BATCH_SIZE rollout to remaining racks (ETA 20m)
- Maria: monitor p95/p99 dashboards, create alerts for slab_frag_pct > 40%
- Jamal: prepare slab compaction runbook and estimate downtime/impact for next maintenance window
- Sarah: coordinate customer comms + postmortem owner assignment

alex: starting final rollout now.

incident-bot: SLO breach declared for streaming p99 at 08:18 UTC. Severity set to Sev2. Handoff to next oncall at 09:00 UTC.

maria: adding `slab_compaction_runbook.md` link to thread: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/slab_compaction.md

sarah: assigning postmortem to @jamal. I'll draft the customer-facing note after we have full timeline.

jamal: For the record — hypothesis: prefill/decode imbalance exacerbated by slab fragmentation. Prefill bursts allocate many small prefetched entries which don't fit slab_allocator buckets -> increased eviction churn -> decode has to wait on disk/backing-store for misses -> tail latency spikes. Need long-term: adaptive prefetch + slab-aware batching.

alex: roll finished. cluster-wide p99 now 1.1s, p95 590ms. streaming error rate 0.12%.

maria: I'll keep this as monitored for 2 more hours. If stable, we mark mitigated and follow up with a scheduled defrag and longer-term work item.

ops-bot: Next oncall rotation @ 09:00 UTC: @oncall-next. Automatic handoff message queued.

jamal: leaving a few TODOs in the runbook for postmortem: capture prefill histograms, per-tenant hotkey lists, slab utilization timeline.

sarah: thanks everyone. I'll update customers and schedule the postmortem.

alex: closing live triage, moving to follow-up thread for RCA and remediation planning. :white_check_mark:
